subject: anaesthesia
title: Topical Anaesthesia: EMLA Cream, Prilocaine Methaemoglobinaemia, and Cocaine

steps.title: Eutectic Mixture Properties of EMLA
steps.tx: **Eutectic mixture of local anaesthetics formulation** (EMLA) combines 2.5 percent crystalline lignocaine and 2.5 percent crystalline prilocaine in a 1:1 ratio by weight. When these two solid local anaesthetics are mixed together at room temperature, their combined melting point plummets to 18 degrees Celsius (well below individual melting points of 68C for lignocaine and 38C for prilocaine), melting into a high-concentration liquid oil droplets emulsion.

steps.title: EMLA Depth and Timing
steps.tx: **Cutaneous penetration kinetics of EMLA** demand application under an airtight occlusive dressing for a minimum of 60 minutes to achieve adequate dermal analgesia (reaching a depth of 3 to 4 millimeters, sufficient for intravenous cannulation and venipuncture). For split-thickness skin graft harvesting or deep dermatological excision, application must be extended to 120 minutes to achieve 5 millimeters of anaesthetic depth.

steps.title: Prilocaine and Ortho-Toluidine Metabolism
steps.tx: **Prilocaine hepatic metabolism into ortho-toluidine** occurs via hepatic microsomal amidases, cleaving prilocaine into carbon dioxide, n-propylalanine, and ortho-toluidine (o-toluidine). Ortho-toluidine is a potent oxidizing agent that oxidizes normal ferrous iron (Fe2+) in haemoglobin into ferric iron (Fe3+), forming methaemoglobin, which cannot bind or transport oxygen, shifting the oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve sharply to the left.

left.title: Normal Ferrous Haemoglobin (Fe2+)
points: Normal physiological state of circulating iron atoms

right.title: Oxidized Methaemoglobin (Fe3+)
points: Formed by ortho-toluidine oxidation of heme iron

steps.title: Clinical Methaemoglobinaemia Features
steps.tx: **Clinical signs of methaemoglobinaemia** manifest when methaemoglobin levels surpass 10 to 15 percent, producing slate-grey cyanosis unresponsive to 100 percent supplemental oxygen, alongside characteristically dark chocolate-brown arterial blood that fails to turn bright red upon exposure to air. Above 30 to 50 percent, patients develop severe headache, fatigue, tachycardia, confusion, lactic acidosis, and cardiac arrest.

steps.tx: The two syringes in this photograph refuse to match, and the darker one explains the patient's slate grey colour. Blood loaded with **methaemoglobin** stays chocolate brown even waved in air, because its iron sits oxidised in the ferric state and cannot carry oxygen at all. Prilocaine metabolites do this, which is why the cyanosis ignores a hundred percent oxygen mask. A co-oximeter settles the argument the pulse oximeter cannot, and methylene blue stands ready when levels or symptoms demand treatment.
steps.say: Chocolate brown blood that stays dark in air is methaemoglobin, the oxidised iron pigment behind prilocaine cyanosis.

steps.title: Methylene Blue Antidote Protocol
steps.tx: **Methylene blue emergency antidote protocol** acts as an exogenous electron donor: within erythrocytes, NADPH-methaemoglobin reductase converts methylene blue into leucomethylene blue, which non-enzymatically reduces ferric iron (Fe3+) back to normal ferrous iron (Fe2+). Intravenous methylene blue is administered at 1 to 2 milligrams per kilogram of a 1 percent solution slowly over five minutes, reversing cyanosis within 15 to 30 minutes.

steps.title: G6PD Deficiency Contraindication
steps.tx: **Methylene blue contraindication in G6PD deficiency** represents a critical clinical trap: glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficient erythrocytes cannot generate the NADPH cofactor required by NADPH-methaemoglobin reductase to reduce methylene blue into its active leucomethylene blue form. Administering methylene blue in G6PD deficiency is completely ineffective and triggers catastrophic severe acute haemolysis.

left.title: Normal Erythrocyte G6PD Function
points: Hexose monophosphate shunt generates abundant NADPH
Rapid, safe enzymatic reduction of methaemoglobin

right.title: G6PD Deficiency State
points: Total absence of cellular NADPH reducing equivalents

steps.title: Cocaine Unique Vasoconstrictive Ester
steps.tx: **Cocaine unique pharmacology** makes it the only naturally occurring local anaesthetic possessing intrinsic vasoconstrictor properties. An amino-ester alkaloid extracted from Erythroxylum coca, cocaine blocks neuronal voltage-gated sodium channels while simultaneously inhibiting the presynaptic reuptake transporter for norepinephrine and dopamine, leaving excess catecholamines in the synaptic cleft.

steps.title: Cocaine Cardiovascular Complications
steps.tx: **Cardiovascular crisis from cocaine toxicity** produces severe coronary artery vasospasm, acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, and intracranial haemorrhage resulting from massive adrenergic stimulation. Beta-blockers are strictly contraindicated in acute cocaine toxicity because beta-receptor blockade leaves alpha-1 adrenergic vasoconstriction completely unopposed, precipitating catastrophic malignant hypertensive crisis.
